title: 2027 Mitsubishi Pajero: We take a closer look at the returning SUV legend

 2027 Mitsubishi Pajero: We take a closer look at the returning SUV legend
 We check out the all-new Mitsubishi Pajero in Japan
 Marcus De Guzman Features 10/26/2026, 2:43 PM Marcus De Guzman After 5 years away, Mitsubishi has brought back the Pajero. Now sharing its bones with the Triton pickup truck, the latest Pajero comes with seven seats and returns as the brand's flagship SUV offering.
 While most initially thought it would have shared components with the Nissan Patrol, Mitsubishi decided to go their own way in designing and building the all-new Pajero.
 But how does the all-new Pajero look and feel like? Well, we happen to be in Japan and we were able to visit Mitsubishi Motors Corporation's (MMC) headquarters. In fact, there was an all-new Pajero displayed inside their HQ and we were able to take a closer look, inside & out.
 Charismatic Design 
 Starting with the exterior, the all-new Pajero gets its inspiration from the XForce and Destinator. Mitsubishi calls it Grand Charisma, and boy, is it charismatic indeed.
 While the SUV already looks good as it is via press pictures, seeing it in the metal makes us appreciate Mitsubishi's efforts in bringing the Pajero's looks into the 2020s. With a boxy exterior, eye-catching LED headlights & taillights, muscular wheel arches, two-tone alloy wheels, and integrated sidesteps, the all-new Pajero evokes a stylish and confident look without losing its boxy and brawny aura. Sure, the previous generations of the Pajero all had iconic designs, but we reckon the fifth-generation would also become a modern classic.
 High-End Cabin 
 The exterior is nice but purists and enthusiasts may find the overall look divisive. So what about the interior? 
 Well, Mitsubishi demonstrated that they can still make a quality interior for an equally (high-) quality SUV.
 From the supple leather upholstery to the side bolstering on the front seats, as well as the use of quality materials for the touch points and cabin controls, Mitsubishi seemed to have not compromised the fit & finish. Even the quality of the trim pieces and the leather inserts on the door panels can be likened to more premium SUVs from more premium brands.
 Since Pajero is the flagship, Mitsubishi made sure it has high level of amenities, such as memory seats for the top-of-the-line models, particularly in the Super Exceed for the Japanese market. It also comes with a power-adjustable steering column for easier driver's seat adjustment. Speaking of seats, the Pajero Super Exceed comes with quilted leather seats with a tan finish, which further gives the SUV its premium look & feel. There are even grab handles on the driver & front passenger sides of the dashboard for easier ingress/egress, while still giving the Pajero its rugged yet functional design. They even have the "PAJERO" name spelled out for all to see.
 Fans of the triple gauge cluster will be happy as as Mitsubishi brought it back... albeit digitally. With a few presses on the touchscreen, you can have the altimeter (altitude), clinometer (pitch and roll), as well as the compass on full display. And despite having a large screen on the center dash, Mitsubishi still put a dedicated panel for the climate control and HVAC. The result is an ergonomic and easy-to-use climate control panel.
 What I'm not too sure of inside the all-new Pajero was the use of a new "push and pull" style gear selector. Yes, it serves a purpose but the fan in me wished it had a typical PRNDL type gear shifter. At least the Pajero comes with paddle shifters as standard in the high-end variants.
 Seating in the back 
 Those who will seat in the back will be happy to know the second row is equally comfortable and comes with some nifty features, like fast-charging USB-C ports and a 100V power socket. Depending on the available accessories, Mitsubishi can even put rear tray tables for rear passengers to use.
 We also got to try the third-row seats in the all-new Pajero. While getting in them will mostly be reserved for younger passengers, I'n happy to report that it can easily fit full-sized adults. Thanks to the reclining third-row backrests and the sliding second row seats, I was able to fit my 5'7 frame in the very back. There's also plenty of headroom, thanks to the boxy roof. 
 Super Select 4WD II 
 In true Pajero fashion, the range-topping model comes with the brand's signature Super Select II 4WD system with various drive modes and a center locking differential
 It comes with 2H (2WD High), 4H (4WD High), 4HLc (4WD High center locked diff), and 4LLc (4WD Low center locked diff). It is then complemented by the Super-All Wheel Control (S-AWC), whicb combines the 4WD system with Active Yaw Control (AYC) and active stability & traction control with anti-lock brakes. The result is better peace of mind when going over rough and unpredictable terrains.
 Last but not least are the drive modes, which include: Normal, Eco, Gravel, Snow, Mud, Sand, and Rock.
 Did Mitsubishi get it right? 
 With Mitsubishi Motors reportedly looking at selling the all-new Pajero in the Philippines for PHP 4.5 million, it carries quite the steep price. In fact, the Pajero is priced significantly less in Thailand.
 Sure, the all-new Pajero is made in Thailand, but it will be a global model that will also be available in major markets like Japan, Australia, and more. With that, it's not surprising Mitsubishi made sure the all-new Pajero carries a premium flagship quality.
 While some might say it's just a fancier Montero Sport with the looks of the Destinator, our first impression of the Pajero's cabin and design makes us think Mitsubishi gave it plenty of thought when it comes to overall fit & finish. After all, the all-new Pajero carries Mitsubishi's heritage and is a favorite among fans and enthusiasts.
 The all-new Pajero is set to become available in Japan, which means the Philippine market may likely get it around next year. Perhaps the only question now is, can Mitsubishi Motors Philippines Corporation (MMPC) still lower its reported price of PHP 4.5 million?
